# Phase Two — Architecture, Five Alternatives, and Critique

## Five competing architectures

### A — Put Create into the route registry
Pros: visible in every mobile dock. Cons: creation is not a destination, active-route semantics become false, history/back behavior becomes confused. Rejected.

### B — Floating action disconnected from app state
Pros: easy markup. Cons: loses alias/Heichel/Series context and duplicates URL logic. Rejected.

### C — Persistent internal creator action owned by Social Creation
Pros: reuses `creatorUrl()`, keeps route model pure, can render both mobile and home launchers from one state snapshot, remains internal-only. Chosen.

### D — Embed the full composer inside Social Hub
Pros: fewer page transitions. Cons: duplicates a mature composer, creates a huge scope explosion, breaks ownership boundaries. Rejected.

### E — Move the entire deep creator rail to Home
Pros: all options visible. Cons: overwhelms phone first paint and removes progressive disclosure. Rejected.

## Chosen shape
Extend the existing creator-launch domain with a small persistent launcher view/controller. It owns a standard-post doorway on the shell and can strengthen Home without altering navigation route semantics. The existing deep creator rail remains in Exact Interaction for advanced intents. Styling is split into mobile launcher, home creation surface, and context chips so no single stylesheet becomes a dumping ground.

## Twenty-five improvements over phase one
1. Reuse `creatorUrl()` instead of QuickActions string construction for standard posts where possible.
2. Keep Create outside `MobileNavigationPolicy`.
3. Keep the four mobile primary routes unchanged.
4. Add one persistent shell anchor with a stable ID and `data-quick-action`/creator semantics.
5. Make the persistent launcher hidden on wide desktop when Home already provides the prominent surface, unless geometry proves otherwise.
6. Reserve bottom safe-area space so content cannot hide behind fixed controls.
7. Give Create a text label, not icon-only ambiguity.
8. Put icon and label inside one bounded action vessel.
9. Ensure focus-visible outline sits above fixed UI.
10. Use `aria-label` or semantic text where the visual icon is decorative.
11. Preserve a no-alias path to composer instead of disabling Create.
12. Represent current context as styled chips rather than loose diagnostic strings.
13. Use overflow-wrap/min-inline-size protections on long context values.
14. Make Home creation surface visually primary before pulse metrics.
15. Keep metrics grouped in cards and never turn their labels into naked text.
16. Keep secondary quick actions visually subordinate to the Post CTA.
17. Preserve Ask Question and Exact Interaction paths.
18. Avoid any external-provider names, icons, toggles, promises, or settings.
19. Add structural contract tests for persistent creator markup.
20. Add creator URL/state contract tests for shell launcher context.
21. Add style ownership tests for every new class.
22. Add mobile geometry/browser witness for dock/launcher overlap.
23. Add focus/keyboard witness where browser tooling supports it.
24. Run the existing Social Hub test suite before and after implementation.
25. Read all touched files in full and compare planned vs actual before declaring completion.

## Risk graph
Persistent launcher → fixed positioning → safe-area collision risk → mobile geometry test.
Persistent launcher → canonical creator URL → state render timing risk → existing creation assembly/presenter integration.
Home redesign → existing DOM IDs → controller compatibility risk → preserve IDs + shell contract tests.
New classes → local style ownership → style contract tests.
Responsive hierarchy → legacy v2/v3 CSS → specificity/cascade risk → inspect browser computed geometry and use narrow owner-specific selectors.

## Architectural principle
The Awtsmoos is one while routes and deeds are distinct vessels; Awtsmoos.com should never lie by calling a deed a destination. Creation will hover near the thumb as an action, Home will invite it clearly, and the deeper creator rail will remain the chamber for richer forms.
